ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, statutory auditors and senior payroll officers against (i) consolidated EU financial sanctions lists (Council Regulations (EU) 269/2014 and 833/2014 and all amendments), implementing UN Security Council resolutions in Spain; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists applied as group policy and as a contractual requirement of payment partners (Wise and local payroll rails); (iv) domestic PEP sources under art. 14 Ley 10/2010 and arts. 12-15 Real Decreto 304/2014, including family members and known close associates, requiring enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for PEP relationships; and (v) BORME, Registro Mercantil and insolvency or director-disqualification registries. Screening results must be evidenced in the AML file at pre-incorporation and refreshed within 30 days before execution of the notarial deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Sección de Denominaciones Sociales, via the electronic channel of the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España (CORPME); portal: https://www.rmercantil.es (Certificación de Denominación Social / Sede Electrónica del RMC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination must be written using the 27-character Spanish alphabet including diacritics; foreign scripts and non-Latin characters are rejected and must be phonetically transliterated into Spanish Latin script; the corporate legal form (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada or S.L.) must be appended; the name must not coincide with or be phonetically or graphically identical to any existing denomination in the RMC and must not suggest public authority (arts. 408-409 Ley de Sociedades de Capital; arts. 404-407 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, Real Decreto 1784/1996).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On RMC rejection, the applicant may (1) immediately request a fresh RMC negative-name certificate through the same notarial channel as the primary practical remedy, triggering a new 180-day reservation period; (2) within one month of notification, file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) under arts. 121-122 Ley 39/2015, attaching the RMC rejection response and a legal memorandum addressing non-similarity and lawful proprietary use; (3) if the DGRN denies the appeal or is deemed to have denied it, file a recurso contencioso-administrativo before the Audiencia Nacional within two months; (4) alternatively seek judicial review of the DGRN resolution before the competent commercial court. The applicant is expressly permitted to list alternative denominations (first, second and third choice) in the same request to reduce rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional and restricted. The registered office (domicilio social) under art. 9 Ley de Sociedades de Capital must be a physical Spanish address where statutory mail, tax notices and legal process may be served and where management is administratively situated; pure virtual-office or post-office-box addresses are not acceptable for SL incorporation or for obtaining the AEAT NIF and TGSS employer registration code. Serviced or co-working offices with a documented right-of-use are tolerated, but the EOR must demonstrate actual operational substance at the declared address, including management presence, payroll records, personnel files and accounting archives; failure to do so creates risk of administrative domicile re-siting orders (art. 283 Ley de Sociedades de Capital) and AML commercial-substance questions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 20%-35% probability of an unannounced AEAT, TGSS or labor inspection visit within the first 12 months of payroll operation for a low-risk standard EOR; the likelihood rises above 60% where the declared registered office is a virtual or shared-agent-only space. AEAT (NIF and payroll tax compliance), TGSS (social security enrolment and employer Código de Cuenta de Cotización), SEPBLAC (AML file verification) and the Labor Inspectorate (ITSS) may each conduct on-site checks without prior notice; cross-border EOR data requests are handled through EU mutual-assistance channels and Spanish data-protection rules (Ley Orgánica 3/2018 and EU General Data Protection Regulation).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC'): arts. 4 (minimum share capital), 9-10 (registered office), 20-22 (deed of incorporation), 33 (registration in the Mercantile Registry) and 62 (bank-deposit certificate for cash contributions); Royal Decree 1796/2010, de 30 de diciembre, for private employment agencies (ISIC 7810).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil with territorial competence over the registered office; denominational name certificate obtained from the Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary and subsequently registered (inscripción) in the Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with the Certificado de Denominación Social and the bank payment certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at the execution of the deed; cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the statutory deposit certificate annexed to the deed; instalment payments are not available for the SL and no escrow account is required by Spanish law; a single-shareholder SL (SLU) is permitted and must be declared in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE CITY OF MADRID, SPAIN, the incorporators unanimously PASS: FIRST: each subscribed share is declared fully paid, the statutory bank certificate attached; the share capital is EUR 3,000, fully-paid limited-liability shares. SECOND: the company adopts registered office at [address], Madrid ES-28000, its actual administration centre. THIRD: [A] and [B] are appointed joint Directors; [C] is appointed Secretary. FOURTH: the Directors are jointly authorized to execute the deed, obtain the provisional Tax ID, and file all Mercantile Registry and labour-authority registrations required for the employment placement and EOR activities. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online through the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the denominational certificate request through the online registry portal listing up to three proposed names; the Registro Mercantil Central verifies absence of identical or confusing denominations and issues the Certificado de Denominación Social; the certificate is valid for three months (renewable once) and must be quoted in the deed.
required_dossiers: Two or three alternative corporate names
Brief object clause (ISIC 7810 staffing / EOR activities)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is objected for similarity or confusion, resubmit with alternative names after the statutory cooling period; the issuance suspension may be cured by written clarification of the difference in the activity object.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Deposit and Bank Payment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the bank to open a provisional corporate account in the name of the future SL (or an in-block deposit account); deposit at least EUR 3,000; request the statutory Certificado de Desembolso stating that the funds are blocked for the company; annex the certificate to the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Identity and NIE of shareholders and directors
Corporate existence and legalization documents for any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due-diligence queries, submit the ownership chain and lawful source of funds evidence; if deposit is refused, open the account at another Banco de España-regulated entity and obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notaría) in the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators or their duly authorized representatives appear before the notary with the name certificate, the bank payment certificate, the lease of the registered office and the draft Articles of Association; the notary verifies capacity, capital payment and legal object, reads the deed and executes it; the 'primera copia' is issued for registration and submitted telematically to the tax office and the Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled powers of attorney if any incorporator is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the legalization of foreign powers or the bank certificate, substitute the exhibit or execute a complementary notarial instrument amending the deed before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Delegación de Hacienda with competence over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days of executing the deed, file Form 036 (Declaración Censal) telematic or in person presenting the first-certified copy of the deed not yet registered; request the provisional NIF valid for six months; after Mercantile Registry inscription the provisional NIF is replaced by the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the deed
NIE or passport of the director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT application is rejected for formal defects, correct and resubmit the censal declaration; if the provisional NIF expires pending registry, renew by evidencing the pending inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered-office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the 'primera copia' of the deed, the provisional NIF application and Form 036 to the Registry within one month of the deed; the Registrador de la Propiedad y Mercantil examines the deed, confers legal protection over the company's name and capital, and orders inscription; the registration certificate is returned to the parties and to the AEAT.
required_dossiers: Primera copia of the Escritura Pública
Evidence of payment of registry aranceles fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a suspension or refusal (nota de calificación), cure the cited defects by a notarial rectification or supplementary agreement within the legal term; contested qualifications may be appealed (recurso gubernativo) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF and Social Security Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file a fresh Form 036 to convert the NIF to definitive; register the company as employer in TGSS to obtain the Código de Cuenta de Cotización (CCC); and enrol in the RED system to file payroll (RLC) and staff movements; the CNAE 7810 activity must be declared for labour statistics and supervision.
required_dossiers: RED access agreement and electronic certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve discrepancies on address or CNAE classification by presenting the registry certificate; if RED electronic enrolment fails, file payroll registrations through the assistance service pending technical resolution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); the official online portal is the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains a Spanish tax identification number (NIF), ordinarily through the incorporation process and the notary's provisional-NIF application, followed by confirmation of the definitive NIF with the AEAT. The SL must file Modelo 036 to register in the AEAT census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents before commencing taxable activity. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment that must register for Spanish VAT generally applies for a Spanish NIF using Modelo 036 and supplies evidence of its legal existence, foreign tax registration, representation and Spanish taxable activity; documents may require apostille or legalization and a sworn Spanish translation. A non-EU-established taxable person may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative, subject to applicable exceptions and international agreements. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 is required where the business needs to use a Spanish VAT number for qualifying intra-Community transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SL is generally a separate Spanish corporate income tax taxpayer; no US-style check-the-box election is available to classify it as a partnership or disregarded entity. Spanish tax law provides specific elections for regimes such as tax consolidation and certain special regimes, subject to eligibility and formal requirements. Spanish anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement applicable EU and OECD measures; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA). The Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla are outside the Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold exempts a business carrying out taxable Spanish VAT activities from registration. A taxable person must register when required by the nature and commencement of its Spanish taxable activity; non-established businesses generally have no small-business registration threshold for taxable supplies in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require prior real-time tax-authority clearance of every VAT invoice. Businesses within the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) regime must electronically report specified invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory timing rules and exceptions. SII generally applies to large businesses exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, VAT groups and taxpayers registered for monthly VAT refunds. The VERI*FACTU and other invoicing-system requirements are subject to statutory scope and implementation schedules; they require compliant invoicing systems and, where applicable, transmission or preservation of records, not universal invoice pre-clearance. B2B electronic invoicing is provided for by the Crea y Crece Law, with implementation dependent on the applicable implementing rules and phased commencement. Confirm current scope and effective dates with the AEAT before deployment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union are generally exempt with a right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory conditions are met and the supplier retains objective evidence of export and, where relevant, the exporter's or purchaser's status. Intra-Community supplies may qualify for exemption with a right to deduct only if the substantive conditions are met, including transport to another Member State, the customer's valid VAT identification number and required reporting. Cross-border services are not automatically zero-rated: the place-of-supply rules determine whether Spanish VAT applies, and any exemption or non-taxation treatment must be supported by the applicable facts and evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and customs confirmation of exit (including the applicable electronic export-system message)
Commercial invoice and records identifying the goods, parties, destination and transaction
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR or other transport and delivery evidence
Evidence supporting the customer's identity and, for an intra-Community supply, valid VAT identification and required recapitulative-statement reporting
Payment and accounting records; an inward remittance certificate is not a general Spanish VAT zero-rating requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The taxpayer must substantiate the conditions for the exemption and maintain VAT and customs records. If the conditions are not met, the AEAT may assess VAT, late-payment interest and applicable tax penalties, and may deny or recover related input-VAT deductions or refunds. Under the General Tax Law, penalties for tax underpayment can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount depending on the classification and circumstances; separate penalties may apply for recordkeeping, invoicing or reporting failures. Fraudulent documentation may also trigger criminal liability where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (BdE), acting as the Spanish national competent authority for banking supervision, foreign-exchange statistical reporting and AML/CTF coordination, in cooperation with the European Central Bank (ECB), the European Systemic Risk Board and the Spanish Securities Market Commission (CNMV).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full participant in the euro area and does not maintain exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible within the EU single market, subject only to statistical reporting to Banco de España and, in limited cases, national-security / foreign-direct-investment screening. Dividend and interest remittances to non-residents are unrestricted, however the payor Spanish entity must apply withholding tax on Spanish-source payments and the recipient may need tax-residence certification for treaty relief.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender euro or foreign-currency export proceeds to Banco de España or any other Spanish public body, and there is no mandatory conversion percentage. Exporters may retain proceeds in EUR or in foreign currency in authorized accounts. Only ordinary customs declarations and balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations apply under EU and Spanish regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Account (EUR SEPA)
Capital Escrow Account; Operational Account (EUR SEPA)
Capital Escrow Account; Operational Account (EUR SEPA)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for EEA-licensed EMIs is Medium: an EEA electronic-money institution (for example a Spanish-licensed EDE or passporting non-resident EMI) can open payment accounts, issue IBANs and clear SEPA transactions. Offshore non-EEA EMIs have Low viability because they cannot directly access Spanish clearing systems nor open Spanish operational accounts without a Spanish-regulated agent or partner institution. For core treasury operations and capital injections, a tier-1 domestic bank remains the primary structural relationship; an EMI may be used as an auxiliary payroll disbursement rail for low-value cross-border workers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance before the bank is not a strict statutory mandate. Spanish Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014 permit secure remote video-identification by authorized providers and notaries. In practice, most tier-1 banks require a recorded KYC interview (video-call or in-person) with at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) before opening an account. If none of the directors can travel, a representative may be empowered with a notarial power-of-attorney and apostilled corporate resolutions; however some banks may insist on at least one physically present local director or compliance officer for non-resident owned entities. The Spanish SL should appoint an agent (legal representative) with an NIE or local address to facilitate ongoing bank communication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership or foreign parents domiciled in offshore low-tax jurisdictions without substantive economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate registry certificates for the full ownership chain, the Spanish Registro Mercantil certificate certifying the SL's shareholders, an ownership chart, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, board meeting minutes approving the capital injection, source-of-funds documentation and a written explanation of the cross-border EOR business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or digital-asset inflows linked to the equity injection or operational revenues.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank records of the real-money origin, exchange and wallet statements, certified valuations, a clear narrative linking digital-asset disposals to liquidity, asset-declaration documents and tax returns, plus a legal opinion confirming the legality of the digital-asset conversion under Spanish and EU law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared EOR staffing activity and actual transaction flows, such as unexplained high-volume payments to unrelated contractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EOR agreements, payroll calculation records, client invoices, contractor employment assignments, social-security registrations, temporary-work-license evidence (if required), and a detailed funds-flow map showing collection, retention of margin, payroll deduction and final disbursement to contractors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or connected to a sanctioned / restricted jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear PEP declaration, complete background-check reports (credit and sanctions), letters of reference from regulated financial institutions, personal wealth and source-of-funds documentation, notarial verification of identity, and an enhanced monitoring plan approved by the bank's AML compliance unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inward capital injections from a non-resident shareholder, the compliant routing is a direct SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer (or SEPA CT if the shareholder is within EEA) to the Spanish entity's Banco de España-regulated account. Purpose of payment should be stated as equity contribution/investment in capital, using ISO 20022 payment purpose code 'EQUI' (equity investment) or equivalent, with a precise reference such as 'Capital Increase – ES_SL shareholder loan/resolution date'. The receiving bank is obliged to submit the statistical declaration to Banco de España; the Spanish entity and its foreign investor must also comply with Spain's Foreign Investment Reporting (Ministerial Order and balance-of-payments rules) and may file the Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores when applicable. Due diligence requires copies of the board resolution authorizing the injection, the shareholders' ledger, the notarial deed of capital increase (if any) and an updated AML file on the paying bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for operational and trade settlements include: (i) domestic and EEA payroll and supplier disbursements via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Direct Debit (SDD); (ii) non-EUR supplier or partner payments via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers, with strict purpose codes (e.g., 'PAYROLL', 'PROF02' professional services, 'SALE' goods/services, 'DIVI' dividends); (iii) interbank liquidity movements using MT202 COV; (iv) documentary trade transactions through commercial Letters of Credit (sight and usance) issued or advised by a Spanish commercial bank; and (v) alternative multi-cubic execution through Wise's licensed EU entity for low-value international disbursements where local FX conversion is cost-effective, provided the downstream recipient is not located in FATF/OFAC-high-risk jurisdictions. All cross-border payments must pass real-time sanctions screening and be retained with underlying supporting documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/MXN) executed with a tier-1 Spanish bank or an EEA credit institution under ISDA/CSA terms
FX swaps (sale and purchase of foreign currency against euro at two different dates) for short-term liquidity management and roll-over of export/import proceeds
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR vs USD or other fully convertible currencies) for matching long-term loan or operational liabilities
Plain vanilla European-style FX options, purchased for hedging currency risk on known contracted cash flows and requiring appropriateness tests under MiFID II

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally unnecessary and not commonly available for EUR because the euro is fully convertible; NDFs would only be considered if counterparties require a synthetic hedge for illiquid emerging-market currencies where local deliverability is restricted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll withholding and contribution recap return (Modelo 190)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to January 31 following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Informative-return penalty of EUR 150 to EUR 20,000 under art. 198 LGT; under-declared withholdings are reassessed with late-payment interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February 1 to February 28 following the reporting year; mandatory only if aggregate transactions with any counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat administrative penalty of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 for non-filing or defective filing under art. 198 LGT

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ETT staffing-agency annual activity declaration, placement-contract register communication, and financial guarantee re-indexation notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SEPE (Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal) and the competent Labor Authority of the Autonomous Community
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly placement-contract reports due within the first 10 calendar days of the following month; annual activity declaration and guarantee revision due by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 6,000 per infringement under Law 14/1994; suspension of the ETT authorization for repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of corporate and accounting books (Libro de Actas, Libro Registro de Socios, Libro Diario, Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end (by April 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lose evidentiary value in commercial proceedings; the annual accounts deposit will be rejected until legalization is completed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting approval of the annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting (Junta General Ordinaria) and Notary when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 6 months of each fiscal year (by June 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to meet triggers court-convening procedures at the request of any shareholder; unauthorized accounts cannot be deposited, leading to the LSC art. 283 penalty of EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the 6-month period following tax year-end (July 1 to July 25 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% of tax due plus late-payment interest; further penalties of EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 for deficient or false data

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with Modelo 200 (July 1 to July 25); mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per counterparty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat penalty of EUR 1,000 under art. 234 LGT plus interest where material related-party transactions are omitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of audited/approved annual accounts in the Mercantile Registry (depósito de cuentas anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the Shareholders' Meeting (by July 31 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Temporary closure of the corporate file (cierre registral) blocking all registry filings; administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000 per non-deposited year under art. 283 LSC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-ownership (UBO) register update through the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and the Central UBO Register (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial control; otherwise certified with the annual accounts deposit (by July 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative fines under Law 10/2010; the Mercantile Registry refuses registration of the underlying transfer deed until the UBO statement is updated

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required when the SL meets at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above EUR 2,850,000; net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees (art. 263 LSC). Additionally, labor authorities may request audited accounts to verify financial-guarantee sufficiency under the ETT licensing regime (Law 14/1994).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) per RD 1514/2007 as updated by RD 1/2021, implementing Directive 2013/34/EU; simplified PGC available for micro-entities; EU-endorsed IFRS required for consolidated groups and certain regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not require a standalone annual UBO return. The SL must (i) file an updated beneficial-ownership declaration through the Provincial Mercantile Registry within 30 days of any ownership or control change (RDL 7/2021 and RD 609/2023); (ii) attach a complete register-of-members certificate to every annual accounts deposit; and (iii) maintain internal alignment between the central UBO file and the shareholder schedule filed annually. Registry cross-checks any discrepancy as a prior condition before accepting subsequent filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and legal representatives (in the Minute Book and RCD Registry of Directors)
Register of Staffing Placement Contracts (Libro Registro de Contratos de Puesta a Disposicion) - statutory for ETT license holders
Accounting books (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales and Libro Diario) - legalized annually

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 to USD 2,700 per year for a typical Spanish gestoria or corporate-secretarial retainer covering registered office, book legalization, annual accounts deposit, and UBO updates
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,700 to USD 7,200 per audit engagement for a mid-size Spanish SL; higher for EOR operations whose workforce and balance-sheet size cross the mandatory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% statutory rate with incentives for R&D expenditure (up to 200% deduction), innovation, and certain sectors

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 via AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the end of the tax period (e.g., 25 January for calendar year companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must file if having Spanish source income; use Form 210 for withholding if applicable
Calculate 25% on taxable base; withholdings credited

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100 euros per day of delay, with a maximum of 1,500 euros for small companies; criminal sanctions for willful evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends distributed to non-residents (reduced by applicable treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Treaty Residence Certificate) and Form 210 or relevant declaration to AEAT to claim reduced rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% (or 0-19% under treaties); Interest: 19% (or 0% under treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 250,000 EUR (mandatory local file for related party transactions exceeding this threshold)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable to entities performing certain activities such as holding companies, IP holding, or pure equity holding; requires adequate substance in Spain for non-genuine arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false claims for deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish entity without sufficient business operations or substance to justify its existence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 1 million euros, potential dissolution, and loss of tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal liability for tax debts, possible travel bans, and criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering obligations in cross-border staffing operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 2 million euros or 2% of annual turnover, criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification, and potential imprisonment for willful non-compliance
